artworks.title: Heracles and Alcyoneus (kylix)
artworks.description: Attic kylix: Heracles confronts the Giant Alcyoneus — the earthborn who could not be killed on his native soil until the hero dragged him from Pallene.

artworks.title: Heracles Slays Alcyoneus (Paestum metope)
artworks.description: Metope from the Heraion at the mouth of the Sele (Paestum Museum): Heracles kills the Giant Alcyoneus — archaic stone of the Gigantomachy's hardest duel.

artworks.title: Athena against Alcyoneus (Pergamon Altar)
artworks.description: East frieze of the Great Altar of Pergamon: Athena and Nike overwhelm Alcyoneus as Ge rises from the earth — the Giant whose mother-earth bond the goddess must break.

artworks.title: Heracles and Alcyoneus (black-figure amphora)
artworks.description: Cabinet des Médailles amphora: Heracles grapples Alcyoneus — vase-painting's stock image of the Giant Apollodorus ranks with Porphyrion among the greatest of the earthborn.

artworks.title: Heracles and Alcyoneus (red-figure amphora)
artworks.description: Red-figure amphora of the same combat: Alcyoneus as the sleeping or fallen Giant Heracles must finish — not the Pleiad Alcyone, but the Gigantomachy's immortal-on-his-soil foe.

popCulture.title: Pergamon Altar
popCulture.description: The Great Altar's Gigantomachy frieze gives Alcyoneus his most famous public face — Athena's struggle with the Giant now in Berlin.

popCulture.title: Alcyoneus
popCulture.description: One of the greatest Giants — immortal on his native soil of Pallene until Heracles (and Athena) drag him from the earth that protects him.
